nbe161dd4d38.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the events leading to Indian independence?
o: The Attlee Statement on transfer of power came before the Mountbatten Plan
Mountbatten replaced Wavell as Viceroy before the Mountbatten Plan
The Mountbatten Plan was announced on 3 June 1947
The Attlee Statement came after Mountbatten replaced Wavell
nbe161dd4d38.x: The Attlee Statement (20 February 1947) came first; only then did Mountbatten replace Wavell, followed by the Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947) and independence.

n242a9b9f110.s:
Consider the following statements about the dominion-status proposal of 1947:
1. It was suggested by V.P. Menon.
2. It proposed immediate transfer of power on dominion status.
3. It required a new constitution to be framed before the transfer.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n242a9b9f110.x: V.P. Menon suggested immediate transfer of power on dominion status. Statement 3 is wrong: the point was to avoid waiting for a new constitution.

n4fa6aa8b8f1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Constituent Assemblies under the Indian Independence Act, 1947?
o: They could not repeal the Independence Act itself
They could repeal any British law
n4fa6aa8b8f1.x: The Act made the Constituent Assemblies sovereign, able to frame any Constitution and repeal any British law, even the Independence Act itself.

nc074cdb71e6.s: Which of the following pairs of Ambedkar's organisations and years is correctly matched?
nc074cdb71e6.x: Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924) was his first organisation. Samata Samaj came in 1927, the Independent Labour Party in 1936 and the Scheduled Castes Federation in 1942.

nbdefb0d9108.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with its year?
nbdefb0d9108.x: The Independent Labour Party was founded in 1936, not 1930. The Bole Resolution was 1923, Manusmriti Dahan 25 December 1927 and Kalaram Temple Satyagraha 1930.

new.s: Direct Action Day was observed by the Muslim League on:
new.x: Direct Action Day was 16 August 1946; 29 July 1946 was the date the League called for Direct Action.

new.s: The riots of Direct Action Day, known as the 'Great Killings', began in which city?
new.x: Riots began in Calcutta (the Great Calcutta Killings) and spread to Noakhali, Bihar and north India.

new.s: On which date did the Muslim League call for 'Direct Action'?
new.x: The League withdrew its acceptance of the Cabinet Mission Plan and called for Direct Action on 29 July 1946; the Day itself was 16 August 1946.

new.s: The first Interim Government was formed on:
new.x: The first Interim Government was formed on 2 September 1946, shortly after Direct Action Day.

new.s: Each Radcliffe Boundary Commission consisted of how many judges besides the chairman?
o: Two Congress and two League nominees
Three Congress and three League nominees
One Congress and one League nominee
new.x: Each commission had 2 Congress and 2 League nominee judges, with Sir Cyril Radcliffe chairing both.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Radcliffe Boundary Commissions?
o: They were formed by Mountbatten on 30 June 1947
There were two, for Punjab and Bengal
The award was published before independence
new.x: The Radcliffe award was ready on 12 August but published on 17 August 1947, after independence; the other statements are correct.

new.s: Under the Mountbatten Plan, power was transferred on the basis of the:
new.x: Armed forces were divided and power was transferred on the basis of the Government of India Act 1935.

new.s: After Partition, the struggle against Portuguese rule in Goa ended with:
new.x: The struggle against the Portuguese continued after 1947 and ended with Operation Vijay.

new.s: Who wrote 'Train to Pakistan'?
new.x: Train to Pakistan is by Khushwant Singh.

new.s: 'Freedom at Midnight' was written by:
new.x: Freedom at Midnight is by Larry Collins and Dominique Lapierre.

new.s: 'The Man Who Divided India' was written by:
new.x: Rafiq Zakaria wrote The Man Who Divided India; Lohia wrote Guilty Men of India's Partition.

new.s: Under the Mountbatten Plan, the princely states were given the option to:
o: Remain independent, or join India or Pakistan
Join India or Pakistan only, with no third option
Join only the dominion they bordered
new.x: Paramountcy lapsed and states could join India or Pakistan; there was no third option of remaining independent.

new.s: Which areas were the only ones to hold referendums under the Mountbatten Plan?
new.x: Referendums were held only in NWFP and Sylhet (Assam); Punjab and Bengal decided through their assemblies, and Sindh decided on its own.

new.s: The partition resolution accepted by the AICC in June 1947 was moved by:
new.x: At the AICC, Delhi (14/15 June 1947), the partition resolution was moved by Govind Ballabh Pant under President J.B. Kripalani.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mountbatten Plan:
1. The Punjab and Bengal Assemblies were to meet in two groups and vote on partition.
2. Sylhet joined East Pakistan after a referendum.
3. It permitted a common Governor-General for both dominions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are correct: the two assemblies voted in two groups, Sylhet joined East Pakistan by referendum, and a common Governor-General was permitted (Pakistan chose Jinnah).

new.s: The United Bengal plan of 1947 was rejected by:
o: Both the Congress and the Muslim League
new.x: The United Bengal plan of Sarat Chandra Bose and Suhrawardy was rejected by both the Congress and the League.

new.s: Plan Balkan of May 1947 was also known as the:
new.x: Mountbatten's Plan Balkan was also called the Dickie Bird Plan; Nehru rejected it as Balkanisation.

new.s: After the lapse of paramountcy in 1947, how many princely states were free to accede to India or Pakistan?
new.x: Paramountcy lapsed and the 565 princely states were free to accede to India or Pakistan.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Indian Independence Act, 1947?
o: It ended the office of the Secretary of State for India
It gave legal force to the Mountbatten Plan
It denied the dominions the right to leave the Commonwealth
new.x: The Act created India and Pakistan as dominions with the right to leave the Commonwealth, so the last statement is wrong.

new.s: As Governor-General, C. Rajagopalachari gave assent in 1949 to which Act, the first law of free India to receive the Governor-General's assent?
new.x: Rajaji gave assent on 2 April 1949 to the Madras Estate Abolition Act, the first law of free India with the GG's assent.

new.s: Which party did C. Rajagopalachari form in 1959?
new.x: Rajaji, the last and only Indian Governor-General, formed the Swatantra Party in 1959.

new.s: Who assassinated Mahatma Gandhi on 30 January 1948?
new.x: Gandhi was assassinated by Nathuram Godse in New Delhi on 30 January 1948.

new.s: The journal 'Janata', founded by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in 1930, was renamed in 1956 as:
new.x: Janata (1930) was renamed Prabuddha Bharat ('Enlightened India') in 1956.

new.s: In which year did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar start 'Mooknayak', his first paper?
new.x: Mooknayak, 'Leader of the Voiceless', was started in 1920; Bahishkrit Bharat followed in 1927.

new.s: The Scheduled Castes Federation was founded by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in:
new.x: The Scheduled Castes Federation was founded in 1942, not 1954; the Independent Labour Party came in 1936.

new.s: The Republican Party of India, planned by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, was formed in:
new.x: The Republican Party of India was formed in 1957, after his death.

new.s: Which organisation founded by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar contested the 1937 Bombay elections?
new.x: The Independent Labour Party (1936) fought for labour, Dalit and peasant rights and contested the 1937 Bombay elections.

new.s: The Kalaram Temple Satyagraha of 1930 took place at:
new.x: The Kalaram Temple is at Nashik; the Chavdar Tank (water satyagraha) was at Mahad.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kalaram Temple Satyagraha:
1. It was a temple-entry movement at Nashik.
2. It began in 1927, the year of the Mahad Satyagraha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Kalaram (Nashik) was a temple-entry satyagraha begun in 1930 that continued for over five years; 1927 was the year of Mahad.

new.s: The Mahad Satyagraha of 1927 was held at which tank?
new.x: On 20 March 1927 Ambedkar drank water from the Chavdar Tank at Mahad.

new.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar compared the Mahad Satyagraha to the:
new.x: Ambedkar compared Mahad to the French National Assembly of 1789.

new.s: 'Thoughts on Pakistan' (1940) by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was later titled:
o: Pakistan or the Partition of India
new.x: Thoughts on Pakistan (1940) was later published as Pakistan or the Partition of India.

new.s: Which book of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, published in 1948, dealt with the origin of untouchability?
new.x: The Untouchables (1948) dealt with the origin of untouchability; Who Were the Shudras dealt with the origin of the Shudras.

new.s: 'Thoughts on Linguistic States' by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was published in:
new.x: Thoughts on Linguistic States came out in 1955.

new.s: Which pair of book and author is correctly matched?
o: Who Were the Shudras – B.R. Ambedkar
The Problem of the Rupee – Jyotiba Phule
new.x: Who Were the Shudras is Ambedkar's; Gulamgiri is by Phule, while Annihilation of Caste and The Problem of the Rupee are Ambedkar's.

new.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar received an honorary LL.D in 1952 from:
new.x: Columbia gave him an honorary LL.D (1952); Osmania gave the honorary D.Litt (1953).

new.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar became a barrister-at-law from:
new.x: He qualified as a barrister-at-law at Gray's Inn, London.

new.s: Which portfolio did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar hold in the Viceroy's Executive Council during 1942–46?
new.x: Ambedkar was Labour Member of the Viceroy's Executive Council from 1942 to 1946.

new.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar resigned as Law Minister in September 1951 over:
new.x: He resigned on 27 September 1951 over the stalled Hindu Code Bill.

new.s: Which term for the Depressed Classes did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar reject?
new.x: Ambedkar rejected Gandhi's term 'Harijan'.

new.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's remark 'Mahatmas, like fleeting phantoms, raise dust but not the level' was made in:
new.x: He made the remark on 14 August 1931 in Mumbai.

new.s: Gandhi launched the temple-entry movement in Andhra at Siddantham in which district?
new.x: Gandhi launched temple entry at Siddantham, Krishna district, on 17 December 1933.

new.s: The All India Anti-Untouchability League founded by Gandhi in 1932 was later renamed:
new.x: The All India Anti-Untouchability League (30 September 1932) was renamed the Harijan Sevak Sangh.

new.s: At the First Round Table Conference, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar demanded:
o: Separate electorates for the Depressed Classes
new.x: At the First RTC Ambedkar demanded separate electorates for the Depressed Classes.

new.s: Who was elected President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 December 1946?
new.x: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected President on 11 December 1946; Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

new.s: Who was the Constitutional Adviser to the Constituent Assembly?
new.x: B.N. Rau was Constitutional Adviser and prepared the initial draft in October 1947.

new.s: The two Vice-Presidents of the Constituent Assembly were:
new.x: H.C. Mukherjee and V.T. Krishnamachari were Vice-Presidents; T.T. Krishnamachari was a Drafting Committee member.

new.s: After Partition, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was re-elected to the Constituent Assembly from the Bombay Presidency in the seat vacated by:
new.x: His Bengal seat went to East Pakistan, so he was re-elected from Bombay in the seat vacated by M.R. Jayakar.

new.s: Apart from its chairman, how many other members did the Drafting Committee have?
new.x: The Drafting Committee had 7 members: the chairman plus 6 others.

new.s: For how many days did the Drafting Committee sit?
new.x: The Drafting Committee sat for 141 days.

new.s: In the Drafting Committee, T.T. Krishnamachari replaced:
new.x: T.T. Krishnamachari replaced D.P. Khaitan (died 1948); N. Madhava Rao replaced B.L. Mitter.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Drafting Committee?
new.x: Nehru was not a member of the Drafting Committee; the other three were.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Ambedkar's views in the Constituent Assembly:
1. He called the Directive Principles a novel feature, like the instruments of instructions.
2. He hoped Article 356 would remain a dead letter.
3. He called Article 17 the heart and soul of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The 'heart and soul' was Article 32, not Article 17, which abolishes untouchability.

new.s: In Ambedkar's view, India as a 'Union of States' meant that:
o: States could secede by a referendum
The Union is indestructible and states have no right to secede
States are sovereign units that formed a compact
The Centre can be dissolved by the states
new.x: Ambedkar said the Union is indestructible and the states have no right to secede.

new.s: In his final speech, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called civil disobedience, non-cooperation and satyagraha the:
new.x: He said these methods were now the 'grammar of anarchy' and should be given up.

new.s: Ambedkar warned that bhakti or hero-worship in politics leads to:
new.x: His second warning: bhakti or hero-worship in politics leads to dictatorship.

new.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar resigned as Law Minister in September 1951 because of the stalling of the:
new.x: The omnibus Hindu Code Bill stalled in Parliament and Ambedkar resigned in September 1951.

new.s: Which law, passed in 1955 as part of the Hindu Code, introduced monogamy and divorce?
new.x: The Hindu Marriage Act 1955 brought monogamy and divorce; the Hindu Succession Act 1956 made daughters Class I heirs.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Hindu Code Bill:
1. It aimed at monogamy, divorce and inheritance rights of daughters and widows.
2. It was passed as one omnibus bill in 1951.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the omnibus bill stalled and was later passed in parts in 1955-56.

new.s: Daughters were given equal coparcenary rights by an amendment to the Hindu Succession Act in:
new.x: The 2005 amendment to the Hindu Succession Act gave daughters equal coparcenary rights.

new.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar is called the 'Father of the Indian Constitution' because he was the:
new.x: He is the Father / Chief Architect of the Constitution as Chairman of the Drafting Committee.

new.s: Which title was given to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the law-giver of modern India?
new.x: Ambedkar is called the 'Modern Manu', the law-giver of modern India.
